newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Governor signs bill to revitalize waterfronts.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Governor signs bill to revitalize waterfronts.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki Monday said he signed legislation that clears the way for the private sector to invest more than $100 million in revitalizing upstate waterfronts.
A variety of federal, state and local funds will be used to "leverage" the funds provided by the private sector.

Pataki made it plain that the projects, a mix of recreational and commercial development, are driven by his Adminisration's emphasis on expansion. "These projects will create new jobs and economic opportunity for a vital part of this great state," he said, in prepared remarks.
Pataki estimated that the Inner Harbor project will create more than 800 construction jobs and 1,800 permanent jobs.

The governor, who on Sunday started campaigning for a $1.75 billion bond act that goes before the voters in November, also has cited the economic benefits of that measure's plans for purifying the state's air and water.
Buffalo's Inner Harbor, Cherry Farm Park in the town and Tonawanda, and Canal Harbor, located in Tonawanda and North Tonawanda, are the beneficiaries of the new waterfront bill.

Among the government monies that will be used for these projects are $14 million in federal funds for the Inner Harbor and $11.7 million from the New York State Thruway Authority's Thruway 2000 money. The city of Buffalo and Erie County each will contribute $300,000.

Empire State Development Corp, which will run the three projects, will provide $3 million initially for the 57-acre Cherry Farm Park. And the Thruway Authority will give $3.3 million for the Canal Harbor project, while Erie County will contribute $300,000.

The three projects will give the public access to the waterfronts in the Inner Harbor, the Niagra River at Cherry Farm, and the Erie Canal, for the first time in several generations, the governor said.

The plans included hiking and biking trails, boat launches, ball fields, and in the Inner Harbor, restaurants, stores, tour boats and a 250-room hotel. The development in the Inner Harbor aims to complement the $127 million Marine Midland Arena, the new home of the Buffalo Sabres, a National Hockey League team.
